reasoning: The three findings of the first round are answered in the artifacts — D1 weighs and rejects the pointer-only form, D3 deletes `.claude/rules/mindset.md` into the new `CLAUDE.md`, the docs claims carry page URLs with verbatim sentences, and the spec's rationale clause is gone while `.claude/rules/` and the goal tokens are now asserted — and every remaining class holds.

simpler.evidence: design.md D1 now weighs the cheapest form first — goal function plus one line that `principles.md` binds, about 0.4 KB and drift-proof — and rejects it with a reason that the scenarios need: it leaves the working agent no principle content unless it opens 13 KB, which is the pointer `openspec/config.yaml` already gives this repository while the gap of #315 persists; the seven lines are what lets an agent recognise a §V moment. The fuller alternatives (all of `principles.md`, a `SessionStart` hook, a plugin rule) stay rejected on cost or support. D3 now deletes `.claude/rules/mindset.md` instead of leaving a file of pointers at launch, moving its two pointers into the always-load `CLAUDE.md` of D4; nothing else in the repository reads it (`git grep mindset` outside `openspec/changes` finds only the fixture path at `tests/publisher/test_memory_checkpoint.py:59`), and `.claude/rules` keeps `workflow.md` and `testing.md`, so the non-empty-scope guards (`tests/agent_process/test_doc_links.py:84`, the sibling header and narrative scopes) stay green. D5 keeps the change script-free.

replaced.evidence: One replaced input: the review contract's policy source, `AGENTS.md` → `CLAUDE.md` and `.claude/rules/` (`.agent-process/REVIEW_CONTRACT.md:6-10`, prompt at `.github/workflows/reusable-agent-review.yml:105`, both edited in task 2.2). catcher.evidence: Catchers and the step each is reached at. The two new publisher tests run under `python .agent-process/scripts/ci_check.py`, the `test` of `.github/agent-process-quality.json`, whose `check_pytest` (`.agent-process/scripts/ci_check.py:249`) collects `tests/publisher`: task 3.2 locally and the `agent-process / quality` check on every pushed head. A wrong form of the new sections is caught in the same runs that tasks 2.1 and 2.2 name: `tests/publisher/test_plugin.py:106` rejects a markdown link that leaves the skill directory (hence the relative `principles.md#…` rule of 2.1), `tests/publisher/test_planning_workflow.py:284-299` rejects `AGENTS.md` and the other absent tokens anywhere before `## Install`, and `tests/agent_process/test_doc_links.py::test_every_internal_link_resolves` catches a pointer moved into `CLAUDE.md` whose path or `SKILL.md` anchor does not resolve — which is why 2.1 lands the anchors before 2.2 moves the pointers. The one gap left uncaught, wording drift between the core and `principles.md`, is stated plainly in Risks: the test derives the § anchors from `principles.md`, so a renamed or added principle fails, and nothing but the Governance line (which the core repeats) resolves a wording conflict.
